description: The public API surface every implementation exposes, and nothing more (decision #23). This is the axis that had no gate: the rule was enforced for BONEMESH_* tunables, message types and corpus schemas, but nothing asked whether a port exposes a method the protocol never denoted. That is exactly how a public broadcast() lived in one implementation alone through the whole 8x7 corpus grid run twice, specsrc, the 49-cell matrix and tiers 5-10, and was caught only by a human diffing two ports method-for-method. Names differ per language because idiom differs, so the mapping is spelled out rather than inferred: a check that guessed names would fail on SendM and routes and be turned off within a week.

php.serve: PHP has no threads, so the caller must pump the event loop; decision #23 names this as the carve-out for what a language forces on a port, and it is the only member of that carve-out with an API cost.

notes.internal-by-convention: Each port marks a reachable-but-not-API seam its own way and interop/api-surface.sh honours the marker: Go keeps it unexported, Java package-private, Rust #[doc(hidden)], Elixir @doc false, JS and Python a leading underscore, PHP an @internal docblock. A check that ignored those would report Rust's send_with_ttl and rekey_epoch, which carry an explicit 'Not API' rationale citing decision #23.
notes.constructors: A language's own construction ceremony is not a capability: PHP's __construct and Elixir's GenServer callbacks are filtered by the extractor, not listed here.
